questions.question: Write a SQL query to find duplicate users
questions.context: Mid-level DS interview at fintech company

follow_ups.text: What if you needed to find users who created duplicate accounts across different time periods?
follow_ups.intent: test understanding of time-based aggregation

follow_ups.text: How would you optimize this for a table with 100M rows?
follow_ups.intent: test production thinking (indexing, query planning)

follow_ups.text: Should you use GROUP BY or DISTINCT? When would each fail?
follow_ups.intent: test SQL fundamentals and edge cases

questions.key_insight: Duplicate detection isn't just a GROUP BY—it's about understanding what constitutes a duplicate in your business context

questions.question: You need to forecast cash collection for next 90 days. How would you structure the query to get historical payment patterns by customer segment?
questions.context: FP&A / financial planning roles at fintech, B2B SaaS

follow_ups.text: How do you handle customers with zero historical payments or very new customers?
follow_ups.intent: test handling of edge cases and missing data patterns

follow_ups.text: Your query takes 15 minutes on 500M rows. How would you optimize it for daily runs?
follow_ups.intent: test query optimization and indexing strategy

follow_ups.text: What do you do if payment behavior changed dramatically post-COVID? Do you use all history or recent-only?
follow_ups.intent: test judgment on data staleness and recency bias

questions.key_insight: Financial forecasting queries need to handle missing data gracefully and acknowledge that historical patterns may no longer be relevant

questions.question: Write a window function query to find customers' longest gap between payments
questions.context: Analytics roles across fintech and SaaS

follow_ups.text: How would you identify customers at churn risk using this metric?
follow_ups.intent: test translation of SQL output to business insight

follow_ups.text: Your calculation includes refunds (negative payments). Should they reset the gap counter?
follow_ups.intent: test business logic thinking

questions.key_insight: Window functions are powerful for temporal analysis, but the business context determines how to interpret null values and edge cases

questions.question: Write a query to compute cohort retention (e.g., customers acquired in Jan 2024, % still active in Mar 2024)

follow_ups.text: How do you handle customers who were active, churned, then came back?
follow_ups.intent: test definition of 'active' and handling of interruptions

follow_ups.text: Your retention % for Jan cohort is higher than Dec. What could explain this (besides better product)?
follow_ups.intent: test statistical thinking and confounding variable awareness

questions.key_insight: Cohort analysis requires clear definitions of lifecycle events and careful handling of incomplete data (recent cohorts have less follow-up time)

questions.question: Build a churn prediction model—walk me through your approach
questions.context: Standard DS interview across fintech, B2B SaaS, e-commerce

follow_ups.text: Why would you choose XGBoost over logistic regression here?
follow_ups.intent: test understanding of model selection tradeoffs

follow_ups.text: Your model gets 95% accuracy. Is that good? Why or why not?
follow_ups.intent: test business acumen and class imbalance awareness

follow_ups.text: You achieved 92% accuracy but 50% false positive rate. How do you decide if this is production-ready?
follow_ups.intent: test production thinking and stakeholder communication

questions.key_insight: Senior engineers choose models based on business constraints (FP cost, latency, maintainability), not accuracy alone

questions.question: How would you detect model drift in production?
questions.context: Production ML roles, companies with mature ML infrastructure

follow_ups.text: What's the difference between data drift and model drift?
follow_ups.intent: test understanding of failure modes

follow_ups.text: You detect drift. What do you do next? Retrain? Rollback? How do you decide?
follow_ups.intent: test operational decision-making

follow_ups.text: How would you automate this monitoring without creating alert fatigue?
follow_ups.intent: test systems thinking and pragmatism

questions.key_insight: Drift detection alone is useless—you need a decision framework for when to act and what action to take

questions.question: You need to forecast headcount needs for next 12 months. How would you approach this?
questions.context: FP&A, workforce planning at scaling companies

follow_ups.text: Your model predicts 150 hires for Q3, but Finance only budgeted 80. How do you handle this disagreement?
follow_ups.intent: test stakeholder management and when to trust the model vs. domain knowledge

follow_ups.text: Hiring has been paused for 2 months due to market conditions. How does this affect your forecast?
follow_ups.intent: test handling of policy changes and regime shifts

follow_ups.text: Should you use time series (ARIMA) or regression? What are the tradeoffs?
follow_ups.intent: test model selection reasoning

questions.key_insight: Forecasting organizational metrics requires integrating business constraints and forward-looking signals that don't exist in historical data

questions.question: Design a feature engineering pipeline for a cash collection forecasting model
questions.context: Production ML at fintech, lenders, B2B SaaS

follow_ups.text: You have 10,000 potential features (customer behavior, macro indicators, seasonality). How do you select the right ones?
follow_ups.intent: test feature selection methodology and avoiding overfitting

follow_ups.text: A feature (e.g., 'days since last payment') has look-ahead bias. How do you detect and fix it?
follow_ups.intent: test understanding of temporal logic in ML pipelines

follow_ups.text: Your feature 'customer credit score' is only available for 40% of customers. How do you handle missing values?
follow_ups.intent: test pragmatism in handling incomplete data

questions.key_insight: Feature engineering for financial predictions requires careful temporal thinking and business validation—the best statistical features can be meaningless or biased

questions.question: Your XGBoost model trained on 2023 data performs well in test set but fails in 2024 production. What do you investigate first?

follow_ups.text: How do you distinguish between 'the world changed' vs. 'our model is broken'?
follow_ups.intent: test systematic debugging approach

follow_ups.text: You realize interest rates spiked in Q1 2024, which wasn't in your training data. Do you retrain or adjust?
follow_ups.intent: test handling of out-of-distribution shifts

questions.key_insight: Production failures are rarely about code—they're usually about assumptions baked into your training data that no longer hold

questions.question: Explain Type I vs Type II error with a real example from your work

follow_ups.text: In your example, which error is more expensive to your business?
follow_ups.intent: test tradeoff thinking and business impact awareness

follow_ups.text: How would you design your test to minimize the costlier error?
follow_ups.intent: test statistical power planning

follow_ups.text: You run the experiment for 7 days and get p=0.08. Do you stop or keep running?
follow_ups.intent: test understanding of p-hacking and when to stop

questions.key_insight: Statistical significance isn't a binary switch—it's a tool for decision-making, and you need to know what error costs you more

questions.question: You A/B test a new loan approval model. 90-day default rate is 2.1% (treatment) vs 2.0% (control). Is this significant?

follow_ups.text: What's your sample size and how long would you need to run this test?
follow_ups.intent: test power calculation thinking

follow_ups.text: A 0.1% difference in default seems small, but what's the business cost?
follow_ups.intent: test translation from statistical to financial impact

follow_ups.text: Your test window is 30 days, but defaults are observed 90 days later. How do you handle this?
follow_ups.intent: test understanding of delayed feedback loops

questions.key_insight: Financial experiments have delayed feedback and compounding effects—statistical significance doesn't equal business impact

questions.question: Explain Simpson's Paradox with a fintech example (e.g., loan approval rates by segment)

follow_ups.text: How would you detect if Simpson's Paradox is present in your data?
follow_ups.intent: test practical statistical thinking

follow_ups.text: If you see this happening, which statistic do you report to the board?
follow_ups.intent: test judgment and stakeholder communication

questions.key_insight: Aggregated statistics can be misleading—you must segment carefully and question what each number represents

questions.question: Design a real-time recommendation system
questions.context: Senior DS interviews at scale-up / big tech

follow_ups.text: Walk me through your latency budget. Where do you spend it?
follow_ups.intent: test systems thinking and tradeoff awareness

follow_ups.text: Your model training takes 6 hours. How do you keep recommendations fresh without retraining constantly?
follow_ups.intent: test production pragmatism

follow_ups.text: How would you A/B test this system without a madhouse of feature flags?
follow_ups.intent: test operational sophistication

questions.key_insight: Real-time systems are about constraints—latency, freshness, cost—and making principled tradeoffs across them

questions.question: Design a system to forecast cash flow for 1000+ customers in real-time

follow_ups.text: Users need forecasts updated daily. Do you batch or serve predictions on-demand?
follow_ups.intent: test latency vs. freshness tradeoffs

follow_ups.text: A customer's 90-day forecast suddenly drops 50%. Should you alert them? Why?
follow_ups.intent: test judgment on system behavior

follow_ups.text: How would you version your model changes without breaking live dashboards?
follow_ups.intent: test operational maturity

questions.key_insight: Financial systems need predictable, auditable behavior—the model accuracy matters less than explainability and stability

questions.question: You're building an ML intake system for a company with 20+ ML teams. How do you structure it?

follow_ups.text: How do you prevent the system from becoming a dumping ground for half-baked ideas?
follow_ups.intent: test governance thinking

follow_ups.text: Teams want different SLOs (some want real-time, some want batch). How do you standardize without being rigid?
follow_ups.intent: test systems thinking with competing constraints

questions.key_insight: ML infrastructure is really about standardizing decision-making, not just technology

questions.question: Write a Python function to compute feature importance from an XGBoost model, with confidence intervals

follow_ups.text: XGBoost's `feature_importances_` can be misleading for correlated features. How do you handle this?
follow_ups.intent: test understanding of feature importance limitations

follow_ups.text: You want to explain the model to non-technical stakeholders. Would you use SHAP or feature importance? Why?
follow_ups.intent: test judgment on interpretation methods

questions.key_insight: Feature importance is a useful starting point but incomplete—correlated features confound the signal

questions.question: Design a data validation pipeline that catches data quality issues before they reach your model

follow_ups.text: A feature suddenly has 50% missing values. Do you fail the pipeline or impute?
follow_ups.intent: test judgment on data quality thresholds

follow_ups.text: How do you alert data producers (upstream teams) without creating notification fatigue?
follow_ups.intent: test systems thinking and communication design

questions.key_insight: Data quality is a contract between producers and consumers—validation is a conversation, not just a gate

questions.question: Write a Python script to backtest a time-series forecasting model (e.g., cash collection forecasts) against historical data

follow_ups.text: How do you avoid look-ahead bias when building features from future information?
follow_ups.intent: test temporal reasoning in backtesting

follow_ups.text: Your backtest RMSE is 0.05, but live forecasts are off by 0.2. What could explain this?
follow_ups.intent: test understanding of train/test distribution shift

questions.key_insight: Backtesting is hard because you must simulate exactly what the model sees at prediction time—any deviation invalidates the results

questions.question: Your production ML model is degrading. Walk me through your debugging process
questions.context: Senior ML roles, production ML teams

follow_ups.text: Is it data drift, label drift, or concept drift? How do you distinguish?
follow_ups.intent: test systematic debugging methodology

follow_ups.text: You find the issue but fixing it requires retraining on all historical data (very expensive). What do you do?
follow_ups.intent: test pragmatism and resource constraints

questions.key_insight: Debugging production ML failures is detective work—you need clear telemetry and a hypothesis-testing mindset

questions.question: Design a monitoring & alerting system for a critical ML model in production

follow_ups.text: What metrics do you monitor? Accuracy? Fairness? Prediction distribution? All of the above?
follow_ups.intent: test understanding of what 'health' means for different model types

follow_ups.text: You get 100 drift alerts per week. How do you avoid alert fatigue?
follow_ups.intent: test judgment on thresholds and signal quality

follow_ups.text: Should you auto-retrain when drift is detected, or always get human approval?
follow_ups.intent: test tradeoff between automation and safety

questions.key_insight: Monitoring must be specific to your use case—a lending model and a recommendation engine need completely different alerting strategies

questions.question: Your ML model is making unfair predictions (e.g., denying loans to certain demographic groups at higher rates). What do you do?

follow_ups.text: Is this due to your features, or is the underlying data reflecting real but unfair patterns?
follow_ups.intent: test understanding of fairness vs. bias vs. discrimination

follow_ups.text: You can't use 'protected attributes' as features, but the model is still making disparate predictions. How do you fix this?
follow_ups.intent: test understanding of proxy variables and indirect discrimination

follow_ups.text: Removing the bias hurts model accuracy. How do you decide if the tradeoff is acceptable?
follow_ups.intent: test business judgment on fairness/accuracy tradeoffs

questions.key_insight: Fairness is a business and ethical decision, not just a technical problem—you need domain expertise and stakeholder alignment

questions.question: You're deploying a new forecasting model to replace the old one. How do you validate it before full rollout?

follow_ups.text: Do you do a canary deployment (small % of traffic), shadow mode (run both models), or full rollout?
follow_ups.intent: test deployment strategy thinking

follow_ups.text: The new model is slightly less accurate overall but much better for certain segments. How do you evaluate this?
follow_ups.intent: test nuanced evaluation beyond aggregate metrics

follow_ups.text: How long do you need to monitor before deciding the deployment was successful?
follow_ups.intent: test judgment on monitoring windows

questions.key_insight: Model deployment is about managing risk—perfect is the enemy of good enough, and the cost of being wrong changes your decision
